root_cause.text: The md-llbitmap bitmap page reader in `llbitmap_read_page()` failed to verify the `In_sync` state of `md_rdev` members, so it could select a rebuilding spare disk as a bitmap source even though its bitmap contents were not yet valid.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the rdev filter from only skipping `raid_disk < 0` or `Faulty` devices to also skip `!test_bit(In_sync, &rdev->flags)`, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states this omission allowed reading stale or uninitialized bitmap data from spare disks still being rebuilt.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip out-of-sync RAID devices when reading bitmap pages so bitmap data is only read from synchronized members.
intent_record.what: The conditional inside llbitmap_read_page() was extended from skipping devices with raid_disk < 0 or the Faulty flag set to also skip devices that do not have the In_sync flag set, by adding `|| !test_bit(In_sync, &rdev->flags)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, bitmap page reads will no longer consider RAID member devices that are not fully in sync, preventing reads from out-of-sync members and ensuring the bitmap is read only from active synchronized devices.

grouping_result.intent: Skip out-of-sync RAID devices when reading bitmap pages so bitmap data is only read from synchronized members.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds logic to skip out-of-sync/In_sync-cleared RAID members when reading bitmap pages, preventing selection of rebuilding spares with invalid bitmap contents as the source.

candidates.rationale: This filtering condition is the direct cause: it excludes only negative raid_disk and Faulty devices, but does not exclude members lacking In_sync. As a result, a rebuilding spare can be chosen as the bitmap source.
The iteration over all md_rdev members becomes vulnerable because the subsequent eligibility check is incomplete, allowing selection from out-of-sync devices.

vuln_statements.explanation: This eligibility check is the root cause because it filters out only non-array and Faulty devices, but does not verify that the member is In_sync. As a result, llbitmap_read_page() can select a rebuilding spare disk as the bitmap source even though its bitmap contents are not yet valid.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is clearly present in `llbitmap_read_page()`, so the snippet is sufficient. In the source selection loop, the function iterates over all `md_rdev` members and only skips devices when `rdev->raid_disk < 0 || test_bit(Faulty, &rdev->flags)`. There is no check for `In_sync` before attempting `sync_page_io(rdev, sector, PAGE_SIZE, page, REQ_OP_READ, true)`. Because the root cause is failure to verify that an `md_rdev` is `In_sync` before using it as a bitmap source, this function contains the bug: it can read bitmap data from a non-faulty device that is not yet in sync, such as a rebuilding spare. The fix is not present, because no condition like `!test_bit(In_sync, &rdev->flags)` is used to exclude such devices.
